facts: Neogen delivered Q1 revenue of approximately $209 million, up 0.3% year-over-year on a core basis, which was in line with expectations.
The company executed a global headcount reduction of approximately 10% of existing and planned positions, expected to reduce operating expenses by approximately $20 million on an annualized basis.
Adjusted EBITDA was $35.5 million in Q1, representing a margin of 17%, down from prior year due to lower volume, gross margin headwinds, and higher operating expenses.
Petrifilm, which has had a core revenue CAGR in the mid-single-digit range over recent years, experienced a mid-single-digit decline in Q1 attributed to distributor inventory rebalancing.
Q1 free cash flow was an outflow of $13 million, representing an improvement of $43 million compared to the prior year Q1.

The company completed the divestiture of its cleaners and disinfectants business for approximately $115 million in net proceeds, using $100 million to pay down debt with annualized interest savings of roughly $6 million.
Neogen ended Q1 with gross debt of $800 million (68% at fixed rate) and a total cash position of $139 million.

Food Safety segment revenues were $152 million, down 4.6% compared to prior year including a core decline of 1.7%, while Animal Safety segment revenues were $57 million with core revenue growth of 5.8%.
The company expects to realize approximately $12 million benefit from cost reduction actions this fiscal year, with more than half already contemplated in initial guidance.
Adjusted earnings per share were $0.04 in Q1 compared to $0.07 in the prior year quarter, primarily due to lower adjusted EBITDA which more than offset lower interest expense.
Full year 2025 revenue was nearly $2.8 billion, up a little more than 3% year-over-year.

The company expects 2026 annual revenue to be between $2.55 billion and $2.65 billion, with a large commercial payer loss driving approximately $300 million in revenue impact in 2026 versus 2025 and an additional $40 million in 2027.
Fourth quarter adjusted EBITDA was $90 million compared to $102.5 million in the prior year quarter, while full year 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $375 million, up slightly from 2024.
The company expects 2026 adjusted EBITDA to be in the range of $335 million to $355 million, with approximately 60% realized in the second half of the year and Q1 being the weakest quarter.
At December 31, net debt was $1.8 billion, down $315 million from September 30 and down $46 million from year-end 2024, with the company targeting a long-range leverage of 3x adjusted EBITDA.
Sleep supplies sales grew in the range of 8% to 9% for both the fourth quarter and full year 2025.

The continuing operations generated $135 million of cash from operating activities in Q4 and $154 million for the full year, with at least $100 million of levered free cash flow expected at the midpoint for 2026.
Full year cash flow from continuing operations includes $98 million in cash costs to terminate the Rotech acquisition in the summer of 2025.

Net proceeds from the divestiture of the Products & Healthcare Services business of $342 million are included in the December 31 cash balance, with an additional $12 million to $15 million of proceeds expected in the spring from purchase price adjustments.

Patient equipment capital expenditures were $45 million in Q4 and approximately $189 million for the full year, with 2026 expected to decline by roughly $25 million to $30 million due to the large commercial payer loss.
Q3 2025 revenues rose to $78 million from $75.7 million in the prior year, representing 5% growth on an apples-to-apples basis after excluding $1.5 million from divested Stockman's.
Adjusted EBITDA increased 26% to $14.8 million in Q3 2025, and would have been approximately $15.2 million excluding several unusual items.

American Place Temporary Casino achieved record revenue of $32 million (up 14%) and record adjusted property EBITDA of $9 million (up 16%) in Q3 2025, with the customer database growing to over 115,000 people.

The permanent American Place project budget was reduced from $325 million to $302 million excluding capitalized interest, while management maintains conviction in $50 million run rate EBITDA for the temporary facility and $100 million for the permanent facility.
Chamonix revenues rose more than 7% with adjusted property EBITDA improving to positive $2.1 million from negative $0.7 million in last year's third quarter, a $2.8 million swing.
Chamonix table game revenues increased 53% versus last year's third quarter and 296% versus Q3 2023, while slot revenues grew 6% and 161% over those same periods.
The company reduced average FTEs at Chamonix from 373 in Q1 2025 to 325 in Q3 2025, a 13% reduction despite entering the busier summer season.
The company had approximately $40 million of liquidity at the end of the quarter with minimal capital expenditures required until permanent American Place construction begins.

Management estimates only 12-15% of Colorado Springs residents visited any Cripple Creek casino in the past year, with Chamonix having approximately 51,000 unique guests—a number they believe can easily double.

On a trailing 12-month basis, Chamonix EBITDA was negative $4.8 million, but management expects the property to be comfortably profitable in 2026 with easy year-over-year comparisons in Q4 (negative $3.4 million) and Q1 (negative $2.3 million).
Global comparable sales were flat for Q3 2025, with North America comparable sales decreasing 2.7% while international comparable sales increased 7.1%.

The company has identified at least $50 million in supply chain savings by 2028, with $20 million planned for 2026, expected to deliver approximately 100 basis points of 4-wall EBITDA improvement for both franchise and company-owned restaurants.
At least $25 million of G&A savings outside of marketing have been identified to be captured across fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
The company plans to accelerate its domestic refranchising program over the next 2 years, reducing company restaurant ownership to mid-single-digit percent of the North American system.

The sale of an 85-restaurant joint venture in the Mid-Atlantic region is expected to close in Q4 2025, reducing annualized consolidated revenues by approximately $60 million with negligible impact on net income.
Total loyalty accounts reached 40 million, an increase of almost 1 million new members over the last 3 months.
2025 consolidated adjusted EBITDA guidance was revised to between $190 million and $200 million, with North America comparable sales expected to be down between 2% and 2.5%.
International comparable sales outlook for 2025 was raised to a range of 5% to 6%, up from prior guidance.
Total available liquidity was $502 million at the end of Q3, with a gross leverage ratio of 3.4x.

More than 50% of sales come from consumers with income above $100,000, and aggregator channels represent approximately 20% of the business with low teens improvement in total net sales across aggregators.
Q3 2025 total revenue was $196 million, up approximately $1 million versus the prior year.
Prescription transaction revenue declined 9% year-over-year, primarily driven by Rite Aid store closures and lower volume in the integrated savings program with one PBM partner.
Manufacturer Solutions revenue was $43.4 million, representing 54% year-over-year growth in Q3.
Adjusted EBITDA was $66.3 million with a margin of 33.8%, an improvement of 50 basis points compared to the prior year.
The company repurchased approximately 13.4 million shares at an average price of $4.61 per share, totaling $61.6 million during the quarter.
GoodRx ended Q3 with $273.5 million of cash on hand and approximately $80 million of unused capacity under its revolving credit facility.
Full year revenue guidance remains unchanged at least $792 million, with Q4 revenue expected to decline sequentially due to Manufacturer Solutions deals closing earlier than anticipated.
Manufacturer Solutions year-to-date revenue is up approximately 35% year-over-year, which management indicated is a more accurate measure of underlying momentum than Q3's 54% growth.

The company has over 200 brand affordability programs on its platform, with nearly 80 being cash prices, including new partnerships with Novo Nordisk for Ozempic and Wegovy at $499 per month and Amgen for Repatha at nearly 60% off retail list price.
Full year adjusted EBITDA is projected to grow approximately 2% to 6% compared to 2024, with margins roughly in line with the year-to-date trend.
AMERISAFE achieved a 20.5% return on average equity and a 90.6% combined ratio for Q3 2025.
This marks the sixth consecutive quarter of top line growth, with voluntary premiums growing 10.6%, gross premiums written growing 7.2%, and net earned premiums growing 6.2% over Q3 2024.
Net income was $13.8 million or $0.72 per diluted share, compared to $14.3 million or $0.75 per diluted share in Q3 2024.
The company experienced $8.9 million of favorable reserve development on prior accident years, primarily from accident years 2020 and prior.
The Board declared a regular quarterly dividend of $0.39 per share and a $1 special dividend payable on December 12, 2025.
Over the past 13 years, AMERISAFE has declared nearly $50 per share in total dividends, including $12.68 in regular dividends and $37.25 in special dividends.
Net investment income decreased 12.3% to $6.6 million due to lower average investable assets following last year's special dividend payment.
Book value per share increased to $14.47, up 7.1% year-to-date, while statutory surplus grew to $259 million from $235.1 million at year-end 2024.
Renewal retention remained strong at 93.6%, and policy count grew approximately 11% year-over-year.
Year-to-date large losses exceeding $1 million totaled 17 compared to 13 at the same point in 2024.
Compass Minerals redeemed the remaining $150 million of its 2027 senior unsecured notes during Q2, funded from cash on hand, pushing the next significant debt maturity out to 2028.
Q2 fiscal 2026 consolidated revenue was $453 million, down 8% year-over-year, primarily due to lower highway deicing sales.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA rose 3.3% year-over-year to $86 million, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to 19.1% from 17.0%.
Salt segment revenue fell to $383 million from $433 million as tons sold dropped 19% to 4.1 million, though operating earnings per ton rose 21% to $15.85 from $13.10.

Plant Nutrition Q2 adjusted EBITDA jumped 202% year-over-year to $17 million with margin expanding to 25.2% from 9.6%, even after only a partial-quarter contribution from the divested Wynyard SOP operation.
First half fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA reached $152 million, up 32% from $116 million, with H1 margin improving to 17.9% from 14.5%.

Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was maintained at a $224 million midpoint (range $212M-$236M), with Salt segment midpoint lowered to $233 million from $241 million and Plant Nutrition midpoint raised to $45 million.
Total net debt ended the quarter at $639 million, down $119 million year-over-year, reducing leverage to 2.7x trailing twelve months from 4.6x a year earlier.

Liquidity at quarter end was $379 million, including $74 million in cash and approximately $305 million of revolver capacity, and interest expense guidance was lowered to $62-$67 million reflecting the 2027 note paydown.

Management completed new collective bargaining agreements at Goderich and one other site, and flagged a planned dryer/compaction capital project at Ogden to be completed later next year that should add capacity at lower cost and improved product quality.
Q1 2026 bottom-line results came in ahead of expectations despite softer top-line trends, with the company reaffirming its full-year 2026 guidance.

Management quantified roughly $0.02–$0.03 of EPS headwind in the back half of 2026 from oil-related cost pressures, primarily on resin/packaging and distribution, which were not anticipated when initial guidance was set.

The company is virtually fully hedged on its core program commodities for the balance of 2026, but diesel fuel is not hedged (though much of DSD fuel cost is borne by distribution partners, not on Flowers' P&L).
Management reset the dividend, freeing up approximately $100 million of cash, with deleveraging as the primary use and a target of reducing leverage below 3x by the end of fiscal 2027.

Nature's Own was relaunched nationwide with reformulation removing another one-third of ingredients, non-GMO verification, and a 360-degree marketing campaign featuring John Cena, with management cautioning a 6–12 month lag before measurable impact.

Traditional loaf, which represents roughly 38% of branded retail, remains the company's primary weak spot, and management defines success of the Nature's Own relaunch simply as stabilizing volumes in that segment.
Pricing taken late last year has left price gaps wider than desired, pressuring volume share, but where gaps have narrowed in certain channels, share trends are already improving.

Promotional and marketing spend was deliberately pulled back in Q1 to preserve dry powder for the Nature's Own relaunch, with the promotional calendar expected to normalize over the remainder of the year.
Guidance assumes no volume recovery but easier comps as the year progresses, supported by half loaf variety expansion, continued snack and Better For You growth, and SG&A cost mitigation.

FY2026 CapEx guidance of $115–$125 million breaks down to roughly $2 million per bakery for maintenance with the remainder allocated to growth initiatives including product line extensions and productivity projects.
Total company sales for 2025 finished at $17.9 billion, representing 4.5% reported growth or 4.9% on a daily organic constant currency basis.
The company delivered adjusted EPS of $39.48 per share for 2025, representing growth of 1.3% year-over-year.
For 2026, the company expects revenue between $18.7 billion and $19.1 billion, with EPS guidance of $42.25 to $44.75 per share, up over 10% at the midpoint.
Preliminary January 2026 sales were up over 10% on a daily organic constant currency basis, supporting Q1 expectations of around $4.5 billion to $4.6 billion in revenue.
High-Touch Solutions U.S. business achieved approximately 250 basis points of volume outgrowth versus the MRO market in 2025, below the 400 to 500 basis point long-term target.
The Endless Assortment segment delivered daily organic constant currency sales growth of 15.6% for 2025, with Q4 operating margins increasing 200 basis points year-over-year to 10.6%.

Operating cash flow for 2025 was $2 billion, with $1.5 billion returned to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases, and 2026 operating cash flow is expected between $2.1 billion and $2.3 billion.
The company expects 2026 total company operating margins between 15.4% and 15.9%, up 40 to 90 basis points compared to 2025, including a 45 basis point tailwind from the U.K. market exit.
Price contribution to 2026 revenue is expected to be north of 3%, with approximately 2.5% to 3% representing wrap from 2025 pricing actions.
The effective tax rate for 2026 is expected to be roughly 25%, approximately 130 basis points unfavorable versus the prior year adjusted rate due to federal tax law changes.
Q3 delivered 0.5% same-store sales growth with the final 2 months averaging roughly plus 1.5% comp growth, which has accelerated into Q4.
Restaurant level operating margins reached 12.5% and EBITDA margins reached 6.4%, representing improvements of 80 and 70 basis points year-over-year respectively.
The company repurchased 996,000 common shares for $33.2 million during Q3, with a year-to-date total of 1,838,000 shares for $62.4 million.
The Board authorized an additional $75 million in share repurchases, increasing 2025 annual repurchase expectations from $45-55 million to $65-80 million.
Q3 sales reached $330 million, a 1.4% increase versus last year, with restaurant level operating profit increasing 8.8% to $41.3 million and adjusted EBITDA increasing 14.1% to $21.1 million.
Traffic in the last 6-plus weeks is tracking at roughly plus 3.5% year-on-year and close to 9% on a 2-year basis, outperforming Black Box casual dining benchmarks.
Cost of sales was 25.7% in Q3, 90 basis points favorable year-over-year, while gross margin is up 90 basis points and margin after direct labor is up 130 basis points year-over-year.
The company ended Q3 with net funded debt of $64.1 million, comprised of a debt balance of $89.5 million and cash of $25.4 million.
Management expects Q4 same-store sales growth of approximately 2% to 2.5%, which would result in full year comps of approximately 2% as guided.
The company is targeting up to 2 new restaurant openings in the second half of 2026 to pilot a refreshed prototype, having signed 2 leases with additional deals in late-stage development.
Q3 2025 total revenue was $246 million, up 6.7% year-over-year, representing the company's best absolute revenue dollar performance in the last 12 quarters.
Q3 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $155.1 million, reflecting 9.5% growth year-over-year with a margin of 63.1%.
The company renewed all of its top 10 clients for extended terms during 2025, including a previously discussed single client that had been a concern.
Year-to-date pipeline grew by $80 million, representing a 67% increase since January, with approximately 40% of the total dollar-weighted funnel coming from growth areas.
The company expects to book approximately $60 million of incremental annual contract value (ACV) in 2025, with 60-65% expected to convert to revenue in 2026.
Full year 2025 revenue guidance was raised to approximately 2.8% to 3.2% growth, with adjusted EBITDA margin guidance tightened to 62.5% to 63%.
Network revenue grew nearly 15% year-over-year in Q3, while Analytics grew 4.2% and Payment & Revenue Integrity grew better than 7%.

A new commercial arrangement in the P&C business resulted in approximately $5 million of nonrecurring revenue benefit in Q3, with total 2025 benefit expected to be $15-18 million that will not repeat in 2026.
Unlevered free cash flow of $113 million and adjusted cash conversion of 73% in Q3 were the strongest posted in 9 quarters.
The company successfully reduced net leverage to below 8x and narrowed forecasted CapEx spend to $165-$175 million for the year.
Q1 2026 total revenue was $140 million, a 79% decrease year-over-year, primarily due to the prior-year period including $603 million in noncash revenue from the Nuvaxovid APA closeout.
Q1 2026 supply sales rose 139% year-over-year to $33 million, and licensing royalties and other revenue increased 116% to $97 million, reflecting the shift to a partner-driven business model.

Novavax ended Q1 2026 with $818 million in cash and accounts receivables, added $80 million of nondilutive cash including a $30 million Pfizer upfront and a $50 million initial draw from a new $330 million credit facility, and expects to fund operations into 2028.

The company reiterated full year 2026 adjusted total revenue guidance of $230–$270 million (midpoint $250 million), with $119 million recorded in Q1 leaving ~$44 million per quarter on average for the remainder of the year.
Combined R&D and SG&A expenses fell 23% year-over-year on a non-GAAP basis in Q1 2026, with GAAP SG&A down 40%, and the company refined its 2028 non-GAAP OpEx target to a range of $150–$200 million.

Novavax is eligible for up to $425 million in Sanofi milestones ($75M for tech transfer completion, $125M for CIC Phase III initiation, $225M upon U.S. launch) plus up to $250 million per Pfizer product, and reported $9 million net loss in Q1 with a goal of non-GAAP profitability as early as 2028.

The Pfizer partnership includes a $30 million upfront, up to $250 million in milestones, and royalties for up to 20 years from first launch, with potential for over $1 billion in cumulative royalties per $1 billion in average annual sales per asset.

Novavax signed 4 new Matrix-M MTAs in Q1 2026, including one with a top 10 global pharma oncology leader, bringing relationships to 4 of the top 10 global pharma companies with rights to explore over 30 unique indications covering more than half of the projected $100 billion infectious disease/oncology vaccine market by the early 2030s.

Bob Walker prioritized the C. difficile vaccine candidate to enter the clinic as early as 2027 pending an IND-enabling repeat-dose toxicity study and pre-IND FDA discussions, with management estimating peak sales potential of $1.5–$2 billion.

Sanofi's Phase IV COMPARE study showed Nuvaxovid had statistically fewer side effects than Moderna's mNEXSPIKE across all prespecified endpoints, with recipients twice as likely to choose the same vaccine again, while Q1 Nuvaxovid product sales of $10 million reflected completion of Novavax's commercial activity in Europe ahead of Sanofi's takeover for the 2026-27 season.
Revenue of $1.07 billion met the midpoint of guidance and represented a 10% year-over-year increase, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of sequential growth.
Non-GAAP EPS of $1.78 met the high end of the guidance range for Q1 2026.
Plexus secured 22 new manufacturing programs worth $283 million in annualized revenue when fully ramped, including a record $220 million from the Aerospace and Defense sector.
The company now sees potential to meet or exceed the high end of its 9% to 12% revenue growth goal for fiscal 2026.
Q2 2026 guidance includes revenue of $1.11 billion to $1.15 billion (15% year-over-year growth at midpoint) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.80 to $1.95.
The company reconfirmed its fiscal 2026 free cash flow expectation of approximately $100 million despite increased working capital investments.
The funnel of qualified manufacturing opportunities remains robust at $3.6 billion, with Aerospace and Defense Engineering Solutions opportunities at an all-time high.
Capital spending for fiscal 2026 is now expected to be in the range of $100 million to $120 million, slightly higher than previous estimates.
Return on invested capital was 13.2% in Q1, which was 420 basis points above the company's weighted average cost of capital.
The new Thailand facility is expected to benefit overall margins by approximately 25 to 30 basis points in the back half of fiscal 2026.
System-wide RevPAR growth was 0.3% for Q3 2025, with full year 2025 RevPAR expected between 2% to 2.5%.
World of Hyatt surpassed 61 million members, an increase of 20% year-over-year, with membership having increased nearly 30% annually since 2017.
Net rooms growth exceeded 12% during the quarter, or 7% when excluding acquisitions, with the company raising full-year net rooms growth outlook to 6.3% to 7%.

The expanded Chase co-brand credit card agreement is expected to generate approximately $50 million in adjusted EBITDA in 2025, growing to approximately $90 million in 2026 and approximately $105 million in 2027.
Full year adjusted EBITDA is expected to be in the range of $1.09 billion to $1.11 billion, an 8% increase at the midpoint compared to last year when adjusting for asset sales.
Group pace for full-service U.S. hotels remains up in the high single digits for 2026, and full cycle group bookings were up 15% in October.
All-inclusive portfolio net package RevPAR increased 7.6% compared to Q3 2024, with pace for Americas all-inclusive resorts (excluding Jamaica) up over 10% in Q1 2026.
The development pipeline reached approximately 141,000 rooms, an increase of more than 4% year-over-year, with upper mid-scale brands now representing 13% of the pipeline versus 10% at year-end 2024.
Adjusted G&A outlook was lowered to $440 million to $445 million for 2025, with 2026 expected to be moderately below full year 2024 despite inflation and acquisition costs.
The company increased capital returns guidance to approximately $350 million in 2025 and has approximately $792 million remaining under its share repurchase authorization.
Total worldwide procedure growth was 20% in Q3 2025, with da Vinci procedures increasing 19% and Ion procedures growing 52%.
Q3 2025 revenue grew 23% to $2.51 billion, with pro forma earnings per share increasing 30% year-over-year.
The company placed 427 da Vinci systems in Q3, including 240 da Vinci 5 systems, bringing the installed base of da Vinci 5 to 929 systems.
Trade-in transactions surged to 141 in Q3 from 38 a year ago, primarily driven by U.S. customers upgrading to da Vinci 5.
Pro forma gross margin declined to 68% from 69.1% in Q3 last year, reflecting a 90-basis point impact from tariffs and higher mix of lower-margin da Vinci 5 and Ion revenue.
The company used $1.9 billion of cash to repurchase approximately 4 million shares during the quarter, reducing cash and investments to $8.4 billion.
Management raised 2025 da Vinci procedure growth guidance to 17%-17.5%, up from the prior range of 15.5%-17%.
Full year 2025 pro forma gross margin guidance was raised to 67%-67.5%, up from 66%-67%, with expected tariff impact reduced to 70 basis points.
The da Vinci installed base increased 13% to almost 10,800 systems, while the Ion installed base grew 30% to approximately 950 systems.
U.S. da Vinci utilization increased 2% in Q3 compared to flat utilization in the first half of 2025, with almost 90% of da Vinci 5 procedures using integrated insufflation technology.
Q1 2026 net sales increased 37% year-over-year to $180 million, with Vita Coco Coconut Water net sales growing 42% and private label growing 28%.

Adjusted EBITDA was $39 million or 22% of net sales, up from $23 million or 17% in Q1 2025, and net income attributable to shareholders rose to $30 million ($0.50/diluted share) from $19 million ($0.31).
Gross margin expanded approximately 320 basis points year-over-year to 40%, aided by better pricing and lower ocean freight, partially offset by tariffs (final $2M flowed through P&L) and inflation.
Full-year 2026 guidance was raised to net sales of $720–$735 million, gross margin of ~38%, and adjusted EBITDA of $132–$138 million.

Q1 U.S. retail scans for Vita Coco grew 36% in volume with U.S. coconut water category up 31%, while European measured markets grew 63% with Vita Coco up 57%, gaining branded share across all major markets.
Management estimates Vita Coco brand will have grown ~30% in U.S. retail dollars through April (normalizing for club promotion timing), including a ~5% benefit from the Walmart reset.

The Americas Q1 shipment growth was inflated by a major club promotion shifting from April 2025 into March 2026; the company guides U.S. Vita Coco net sales to grow low- to mid-teens for the full year.
U.S. private label net sales growth guidance was raised to 35%–40%, with shipments for a new major U.S. retailer's Tetra Pak private label launch beginning in Q2.
The company expects to operate at 85%–90% of committed capacity in 2026 (above the typical 80%–85%) and is expanding capacity for 2027 and beyond.

Vita Coco ended Q1 with $202 million in cash, no debt, repurchased $12 million of shares in the quarter ($21 million remaining on authorization), and submitted $15.6 million in IEEPA tariff refund claims not included in guidance.

Q1 2026 total revenue and service revenue both grew 2%, with service revenue rising to $130.4 million, and full-year guidance was reaffirmed for service revenue (flat to 2% growth) and OEBITDA of $480-$490 million.

OEBITDA was $116.3 million in Q1 2026, down 5% year-over-year, primarily reflecting a $4.2 million hit from shifting annual incentive compensation to cash, which will have a $17 million full-year impact (OEBITDA would otherwise have been guided to $497-$507 million).
Voice and data revenue rose 3% to $57.4 million, driven by last summer's price actions which produced a 7% ARPU increase, with ARPU expected to remain around $48 for the rest of 2026.
Commercial IoT revenue grew 5% to $46 million with subscriber trends stabilizing, while commercial broadband declined 5% due to ongoing customer conversions to lower-cost backup companion services.

Government service revenue was $27.6 million, and management expects EMSS revenue of $110.5 million in 2026, anticipating the U.S. government will exercise a 6-month extension option at current rates while contract renewal is negotiated.

Engineering and support revenue grew to $40.8 million from $37.5 million a year earlier, driven by expanding Space Development Agency work, supporting another expected record year for engineering growth.

Iridium reiterated conviction that PNT will drive at least $100 million in annual revenue by 2030, with the new PNT ASIC launching in July having attracted over 100 new companies expressing interest and discussions with major GNSS chipmakers about embedding Iridium PNT IP.

The new Iridium 9604 TriMode IoT module (combining satellite SBD, cellular IoT, and GPS) is on track for commercial availability in June 2026 with beta partner testing underway, and 7 MNO agreements have been signed for the Iridium NTN Direct service launching later this year.

Iridium ended Q1 with $111.6 million in cash, net leverage of 3.4x OEBITDA, Q1 CapEx of $30 million, paid a $0.15/share dividend, and projects pro forma free cash flow of approximately $318 million in 2026 and $1.5-$1.8 billion cumulatively through the end of the decade.

Management indicated openness to monetizing spectrum through partnerships (not leasing) for applications like 5G new radio, and is designing a next-generation constellation potentially requiring ~4x more satellites with a target of up to 10x capacity increase, with equipment sales expected at $80-$90 million in 2026.

Record adjusted EPS of $5.20 was achieved in Q3, representing a 25% increase from a year ago.
Trailing 12-month recruited assets reached a record $168 billion, with $33 billion added in Q3 alone.
Advisers representing nearly 80% of Commonwealth assets have signed to stay, tracking toward the 90% retention target.
Run rate EBITDA expectation for Commonwealth has increased to approximately $425 million once fully integrated, with Atria's expected run rate EBITDA increasing to approximately $155 million.
Pricing changes planned for 2026 are estimated to increase trailing 12-month adjusted pretax margin by approximately 1 percentage point.
Core G&A guidance for full year 2025 was lowered to a range of $1.86 billion to $1.88 billion due to cost initiatives tracking ahead of schedule.
ICA yield was 351 basis points in Q3, but is expected to decrease to roughly 345 basis points in Q4 due to recent rate cuts.
Leverage ratio ended Q3 at 2.04x, below initial expectations of roughly 2.25x following the close of Commonwealth.
October organic growth is tracking around 4%, with client cash balances up $700 million in the month excluding $2.4 billion in advisory fee outflows.
BioAtla is in advanced stages to finalize a strategic transaction with a potential partner by year-end.
The company had $8.3 million in cash and cash equivalents as of September 30, 2025.
BioAtla reported a net loss of $15.8 million in Q3 2025 compared to $10.6 million in Q3 2024.
R&D expenses decreased to $9.5 million in Q3 2025 from $16.4 million in Q3 2024, a reduction of $6.9 million.
Context Therapeutics triggered a $2 million milestone payment in October 2025 under the Dual-CAB Nectin-4 TCE license agreement.

Oz-V Phase II data in HPV-positive OPSCC showed a 45% overall response rate and 11.6-month median overall survival versus historical rates of 0%-3.4% ORR and 4.4-month median OS with standard therapies.
BioAtla estimates worldwide peak sales of Oz-V at approximately $800 million in second-line and later OPSCC alone.
The Phase III registrational trial for Oz-V will enroll approximately 300 patients for full approval, with an interim analysis for potential accelerated approval.
Mec-V showed median overall survival of 21.5 months in soft tissue sarcoma patients compared to 11.5-13.6 months reported for approved agents in similar populations.

A patient with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma treated with the Dual-CAB EpCAM T-cell engager achieved a confirmed partial response and remains on treatment without progression for more than 6 months.
Q3 2025 total revenue reached a record $513.7 million, an 8.6% increase year-over-year.
Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2025 was $56.5 million with margins of 11%, while last 12-month adjusted EBITDA reached $217.1 million.
Innovative Pumping Solutions sales grew 11.9% year-over-year to $100.6 million, while Supply Chain Services declined 5% year-over-year to $63 million.
DXP Water now represents 54% of Innovative Pumping Solutions' year-to-date sales, up from 47% at the same time last year.
On a 9-month comparative basis, native energy IPS backlog is up 56.2% year-over-year, though Q3 saw the first quarterly backlog decline (3.3%) in 10 quarters.
Gross profit margins improved 50 basis points year-over-year to 31.4%, with year-to-date margins up 89 basis points versus last year.
Earnings per diluted share for Q3 2025 was $1.31 versus $1.27 in Q3 2024, with adjusted EPS of $1.34.
Free cash flow for Q3 2025 was $28.2 million versus $24.4 million in Q3 2024, with return on invested capital at 33%.
